summary: Register bounded intake completion state before asynchronous work

replay.detail: No replay or durable format change.

schema.detail: No SQL, DDL, index or migration changes.

rules.detail: Admission, canonical and fresh effect authority remain unchanged. Completion marks do not authorize work.

compatibility.detail: Selected active intake items register completion state before initial evaluation. Completions for an initial or failed evaluation select only that item, and completion during successful evaluation remains needed. Unregistered/pruned callbacks allocate no state; a reborn item is new and a callback on an already registered reused name conservatively selects that item.

downtime.detail: No additional interruption beyond normal binary swap; no deployment implied.

manual.detail: No configuration or pass/load budget changes.

recovery.detail: Unevaluated completion placeholders use the existing item map and are capped at 4096 entries, 4096 UTF-8 bytes/key and 1 MiB cumulative key bytes before cloning. Successful evaluation converts a placeholder to normal retained state; complete-roster pruning releases its registration count/bytes. Callback threads never register arbitrary keys or allocate a completion queue. Registration refusal or generation wrap enables conservative global invalidation for missing completions until process restart, without retaining refused keys; completion-version exhaustion also globally invalidates. This exhaustion fallback can still cost whole-inventory evaluation and is not a performance acceptance. Existing successful item/history storage, full-pass safety, physical-mutation/gap limitations and independent fresh effect fences remain. No full-pass under 500 or production savings result.
